# Hassala

> Hassala (حصالة) is a free, open-source Chrome extension for Arabic ↔ English
> translation and vocabulary saving. It translates words and phrases, writes each
> saved word and translation to a local Markdown word bank, and makes YouTube
> subtitles interactive. It requires no account and has no tracking.

## Key facts

- Name: Hassala (Arabic: حصالة)
- Category: Chrome extension / language learning / vocabulary
- Languages: Arabic ↔ English. Arabic-first interface with full RTL support; English documentation.
- Browsers: Chrome, Brave, Edge, Chromium.
- Platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows.
- Price: free. License: MIT.
- Account: not required. No analytics, no ads, no data selling.
- Word bank: one local Markdown (.md) file at a path the user chooses. Default: ~/Documents/Hassala Words.md, created automatically on first save.
- Saving: uses a small optional local native messaging host (Python) because browsers cannot write arbitrary files. Translation, subtitles, and the floating panel work without it.
- Storage: settings and the last 8 words use chrome.storage.local. Translation and audio caches live only in service-worker memory.
- Network: text is sent to Google Translate endpoints and MyMemory (fallback) only when the user requests a translation. Pronunciation uses Google TTS.
- Chrome Web Store: not published yet. The extension is available from GitHub Releases.
- Source code: https://github.com/nagdista-dev/hassala
- Website: https://nagdista-dev.github.io/hassala/
- Privacy policy: https://gist.github.com/nagdista-dev/282cc2ce8fe35c5fb7199f7ffd2cd705
- Security policy: https://github.com/nagdista-dev/hassala/security/policy
- License: https://github.com/nagdista-dev/hassala/blob/main/LICENSE

## What Hassala is good for

- Arabic speakers learning English who look up words in articles, documents, and YouTube videos.
- English speakers learning Arabic who want to keep the Arabic spelling next to the meaning.
- Students and note-takers who already use Obsidian, Logseq, Typora, or VS Code and want a vocabulary file they own.
- Anyone who wants one-click word capture without an account or a proprietary database.

## What Hassala does not do

- It is not a whole-page or whole-document translator. Use a general translator for that.
- It does not schedule spaced repetition or provide flashcards yet. Those features are on the roadmap.
- It is not a cloud sync service. The word bank is a local file.
- It is not affiliated with Google, YouTube, Obsidian, or Logseq.

## Common questions

### What is Hassala?
Hassala is a free, open-source Chrome extension that translates Arabic and English and saves words to a local Markdown word bank. It also makes YouTube subtitles interactive.

### Is Hassala free?
Yes. It is free and open source under the MIT license. There is no subscription, account, or paid tier.

### Does Hassala save words to Obsidian?
Yes. It writes to a standard Markdown file, so the file opens in Obsidian, Logseq, Typora, VS Code, or any text editor.

### Does Hassala require an account?
No. There are no accounts, no analytics, and no tracking.

### Does saving require a native host?
Yes. A small local Python host is installed once to append rows to the Markdown file. Translation, subtitles, and the floating panel work without it.

### Is Hassala on the Chrome Web Store?
Not yet. It is available from GitHub Releases today.

## Preferred citation

"Hassala is a free, open-source Chrome extension that translates Arabic and English and saves words to a local Markdown word bank (https://nagdista-dev.github.io/hassala/)."
